# `silk/http/websocket_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Native WebSocket clients and split sessions over TCP and TLS.

## When to use
Call [`connect`](#connect) to open a client session to a `ws` or `wss` URI. Call [`split`](#split) on a session
over a `NativeTransport`, from [`connect`](#connect) or from `acceptOwned` of
`silk.http.websocket_upgrade`, so that one fiber reads while other fibers send.

## Details
[`connect`](#connect) opens the connection with `acquireOwned` of `silk.http.exchange_native`, then calls
`handshake` of `silk.http.websocket_client`. A `wss` URI uses TLS with the trust snapshot that
you give, and offers only HTTP/1.1 in ALPN.

[`split`](#split) splits the socket, and for TLS the session, so the reader and the writers do not
wait for each other.

## Errors
[`connect`](#connect) fails with the errors of the connection and of the handshake. `OriginError` if the
URI is not a `ws`, `wss`, `http`, or `https` URI.

## Gotchas
- With a host name, the deadline of the options must be `None`, as for `acquireOwned`.
- The session does not close the transport. Close it when the session is `Closed` or failed.

## Examples
### Split an accepted session
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.http.exchange_native { NativeTransport }
import silk.http.websocket_native { split }
import silk.http.websocket_stream { Split, WebSocket }

// Splits `socket`, so a fiber can read with the reader while others send with the writer.
effect fn halves(socket: WebSocket<NativeTransport>) -> Split<NativeTransport, NativeTransport>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  return run split(move socket)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return 0
}
```

Import as `WebSocketNative` with `import silk.http.websocket_native as WebSocketNative`.

## `connect`

```silk
pub effect fn connect<'value>(
  uri: &Uri<'value>,
  headers: &Headers<'value>,
  options: ClientOptions<'value>,
  native: NativeOptions,
  preparedTrust: Option<TrustSnapshot>,
) -> Opened<NativeTransport>
! OriginError | NativeExchangeError | ResolverError | NativeSocketError | ConnectionError | IdentityError | HandshakeError | ExchangeError | RequestError | StreamError | OutOfMemoryError
? &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock | &mut SystemClock | &mut Random
```

Opens a connection to the origin of `uri`, sends the opening handshake, and returns the open
client session.

### Details
`native` sets the socket and TLS options. The deadline of `options` limits the connection too.
`preparedTrust` is needed for `wss`. `headers` are sent with the handshake, as for `handshake`.

### Errors
- `OriginError` if `uri` has no valid origin.
- `NativeExchangeError`, `ResolverError`, `NativeSocketError`, `ConnectionError`, and
  `IdentityError` from the connection, as for `acquireOwned`.
- [`HandshakeError`](./http-websocket-client.md#HandshakeError), `ExchangeError`, `RequestError`, and `StreamError` from the handshake.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer cannot grow.

<a id="split"></a>

## `split`

```silk
pub effect fn split(socket: WebSocket<NativeTransport>) -> Split<NativeTransport, NativeTransport>
! OutOfMemoryError
? &mut Allocator
```

Splits a session over a `NativeTransport` into a reader and a writer.

### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the shared state cannot be allocated.

### Gotchas
It traps if the transport is already a half.
